structure:
One ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-17.md, 20 lines in four pieces: a two-line preamble saying the ruling was given in the overview-and-review build session, answers the review page's wording question (where the prototype names one thing two ways), and replaces the 16 November orchestrator decision to take each question page's own wording; a numbered list of three decisions (1 the exit port, 2 the arrival date, 3 addresses, whose third item carries three sub-bullets for section heading, heading/H1/task row/card title, and validation message); Sam's verbatim words as one quoted paragraph, which is the source the three listed decisions are read from; and a closing two-line paragraph of orchestrator's calls applying the ruling (section numbers stay, the overview row's hint stays, plants takes the same address wording because plants matches animals on these pages). The scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out; the file names no page file, no component and no repo path, and gives no wording for anything beyond the exit port, the arrival date and the addresses section, so it settles only those three wording points and the three applying calls.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, The whole ruling: review-page wording for exit port, arrival date and addresses: Part 1 is the whole source: every line of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-17.md, read in full (20 lines). It is laid out in four pieces, and this part covers all four. (1) A two-line preamble: the ruling was given in the overview-and-review build session, answers the review page's wording question where the prototype names one thing two ways, and replaces the 16 November orchestrator decision to take each question page's wording. (2) Three numbered decisions: 1 the exit port is "Port of exit" everywhere, check your answers included, and "Exit border control post" is not used; 2 the arrival date is "Arrival date at port of entry" everywhere, check your answers included, and "Arrival date at destination" is not used; 3 addresses read the same on check your answers, the overview (task list) and the addresses page itself, with three sub-bullets for the section heading, the heading (H1, task row and card title) and the validation (incomplete-card) message. (3) Sam's verbatim quoted paragraph, which is the owner's own words and the source the three listed decisions are read from: it names "Port of exit", "Arrival date at port of entry", and for addresses "[Section heading] Addresses [H1] Consignment addresses [Validation] Complete consignment addresses" across check your answers, the Overview page and the page itself. (4) A closing two-line paragraph of orchestrator's calls applying the ruling: section numbers stay ("5. Addresses"), the overview row's hint stays, and plants takes the same address wording because plants matches animals on these pages. Covered here: the two framing facts of the preamble, all three decisions with their rejected alternatives and all three address sub-bullets, the three orchestrator's calls, each checked word for word against Sam's quote (what the quote says in so many words is verbatim; what it only implies is inferred, with the statement naming what implies it), and what the ruling leaves open as gaps. The file names no page file, no component and no repo path, and gives no wording for anything beyond the exit port, the arrival date and the addresses section.
